summary: Iteration 224: tested new ENZI @AI in-channel assistant (POST /api/lumi/channels/{id}/ai) and LiveKit live-captions UI. Backend: 12/12 pytest passed (auth 401, non-member 403, empty-query 400, summarize + actions intents return ENZI AI ai_assistant messages that persist, /api/translate/languages returns 60+ langs, /api/realtime-stt/status available=true, /api/lumi/ai/translate ok, LUMI channels/messages regression ok, iteration223 refactor suite 11/11 passed). A dedicated websocket test proves the backend DOES broadcast the AI reply over /api/lumi/ws/{user_id}. Frontend KARAU captions UI fully works (CC toggle, 61 options incl. 'Original (no translation)', French selection, select hides on CC off, no crash). Frontend ENZI has 2 real bugs: (1) the ENZI AI reply never renders live — only after page reload; (2) all markdown in AI replies (bold headings, bullet lists, task checkboxes) is rendered with white text on a white background, i.e. invisible.

minor.issue: Non-existent channel id returns 403 'Not a member of this channel' instead of 404 — acceptable (no info leak) but semantically ambiguous.
No rate limiting / concurrency guard: a user can spam @AI and trigger unbounded gpt-4.1-mini calls.

ui_bugs.issue: Markdown palette is hard-coded for a dark surface (li = text-white/80, strong = text-white, td/th = text-white/*) but MessageBubble renders on an effective rgb(255,255,255) background (verified by walking computed background chain). Result: ENZI AI summaries/action-item checklists appear as large blank gaps — only plain paragraphs (text-slate-900 inherited) are readable. Contrast ratio ~1:1.

Caption language picker uses a native <select> (browser default picker) rather than the shadcn Select used elsewhere; also no visual 'listening/transcribing' indicator so a host cannot tell captions are actually capturing.

integration_issues.issue: After sending '@AI summarize this conversation' the user's own message renders live and POST /ai returns 200, but the ENZI AI reply NEVER appears in the open thread (waited 30s+, twice, for both 'summarize' and 'extract action items'). It only shows after a page reload (verified: 4 ai-assistant badges + correct content after reload). Backend is innocent — /app/backend/tests/test_iteration224_ws_broadcast.py proves the AI frame IS pushed over the LUMI websocket to a single stable socket. RCA: LumiMessenger.jsx opens duplicate websockets (3 WS OPEN observed for the same user in one session) because the WS useEffect depends on loadChannels/loadDms/loadUnreadCounts, and every incoming 'message' frame calls loadChannels()/loadDms()/loadUnreadCounts() -> callbacks re-created -> effect teardown closes the socket and reconnects. Backend ConnectionManager.disconnect(user_id) pops the entry by user_id regardless of which socket closed, so the surviving client socket is removed from active_connections and receives no further broadcasts. The first (user) message arrives before the churn; the AI reply 5-15s later is dropped.
ws.onmessage appends every 'message' frame to the open thread without checking msg.data.channel_id === activeChannel.id — messages from other channels can leak into the currently open thread.

issues: ENZI AI markdown content invisible (white on white)
Because content is invisible, AI messages occupy tall empty vertical gaps (~400px) making the thread look broken
GFM task-list checkboxes render as bare unlabelled checkboxes

action_items: FIX (HIGH): make RichMessage.jsx theme-aware (or use slate-800/slate-900 text on the light ENZI bubble surface) so AI markdown headings/lists/tables/checkboxes are visible.

FIX (HIGH): stabilise the LUMI websocket in LumiMessenger.jsx — remove loadChannels/loadDms/loadUnreadCounts from the WS useEffect deps (use refs), guard against duplicate sockets, and/or make backend ConnectionManager.disconnect only remove the socket instance that actually closed. Verify the ENZI AI reply lands in the open thread without reload.
FIX (MED): filter incoming WS 'message' frames by channel_id before appending to the active thread.
CONSIDER: per-user rate limit on POST /api/lumi/channels/{id}/ai.
critical_code_review_comments: ai_agent.py is clean: excludes _id, validates empty query, 401/403/400/500 paths, uses env EMERGENT_LLM_KEY, sorts last 30 messages and excludes prior AI turns from context.
LumiMessenger.jsx handleSend fires the /ai POST without awaiting and only toasts on failure — no optimistic 'thinking' placeholder message, so a dropped WS frame is completely silent to the user.
ConnectionManager.disconnect(user_id) is not socket-scoped — a stale duplicate connection closing evicts the live one (systemic realtime bug, not only for AI messages).
LiveKitCaptions.jsx swallows every error with empty catch blocks (fetch/getUserMedia/transcribe) — mic-permission or Whisper failures give the user zero feedback while 'CC on' stays lit.

rca_of_the_issue: Live AI reply missing: frontend opens multiple LUMI websockets because the WS useEffect depends on unstable useCallback identities that change on every incoming message (which itself triggers loadChannels/loadDms/loadUnreadCounts). React cleanup closes a socket; the backend ConnectionManager.disconnect(user_id) removes the user's entry from active_connections irrespective of which socket closed, so the still-open client socket stops receiving send_to_channel broadcasts. Since the ENZI AI answer arrives 5-15s after the user's message (LLM latency), it lands in that dead window and is lost; a reload re-fetches messages and shows it. Invisible AI text: RichMessage.jsx hard-codes a dark-surface palette while MessageBubble's effective background is white (verified rgb(255,255,255) via computed background chain).
